newsitem.title: USA: Beverly's CEO sees slower growth ahead.
newsitem.headline: Beverly's CEO sees slower growth ahead.

text.p: Beverly Enterprises Inc's Chief Executive David Banks said Wednesday he expected the company's earnings growth rate to slow in the second half of the year.

"The gains we expect to make during the second half will be somewhat smaller in scale, reflecting the fact that we'll be comparing ... with the agressive results we achieved in the third and fourth quarters of 1996," Banks said in a statement.
Beverly on Wednesday reported its second quarter net income rose to $21.0 million, or $0.21 a share, up 23 percent over last year.
A First Call consensus estimate of 14 brokers put the company's earnings at $0.20 a share.
"Our principal business units exceeded their operating profit objectives for both the quarter and the first half, and achieved significant increases in margins," Banks said.

Banks said the company's overall profit margin for the second quarter (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization as a percent of revenues) was up more than 0.7 percent. He added same-facility revenues grew about six percent over last year.

Beverly said its Pharmacy Corp of America posted double-digit gains in revenues and operating profits in the second quarter. The division's same facility's revenues rose more than 15 percent and the unit's profit margin rose 1.5 percent.
Beverly said its plan to sell the unit to Capstone Pharmacy Services Inc is on schedule to close in the fourth quarter.

The company said its Health and Rehabilitation Services unit improved its operating margin by more than 0.5 percent in the quarter and posted double-digit profit growth from the year-earlier quarter on a same facility basis.

It added the unit's revenues rose nearly five percent on a same-facility basis, but were down slightly in total. It attributed the result to operating 63 fewer facilities (an 11 percent decrease in licensed beds), compared to the year-earlier period.

Beverly said its nursing home occupancy dropped 1.2 percent in the quarter over last year, despite a five percent increase in admissions. The company attributed a six percent increase in revenues per patient day and higher operating margins to the continuing trend of shorter patient stays.
The company said its complementary business units -- Spectra Healthcare Alliance and American Transitional Hospitals -- achieved increased revenues and operating profits on a same-facility basis.
Beverly's stock closed at 16-9/16 Wednesday, close to its 52-week high of 17.
